dedupe_keys.name: hurricane sandy recovery and resilience of new york city transit subway tunnels four years on 2016

description: A trade press account, published by Progressive Railroading in November 2016 with statements from New York City Transit, of how the subway recovered from Hurricane Sandy. Coverage: NYCT subway tunnels, yards and systems in New York City. Event: the storm surge of 29 October 2012 poured saltwater into nine of the system's 14 under-river tunnels, damaging track, switches, signals, power and communication cables, with more than 4.5 billion dollars of subway damage; service returned in three days, but full repair took years. Outcome: a Sandy Recovery and Resiliency Division coordinated tunnel projects, including Montague (259 million dollars, 13-month closure, finished 2015), Greenpoint (93 million), Steinway (29 million), Cranberry, Joralemon and 53rd Street, and a planned 18-month closure of the Canarsie Tunnel at about 1 billion dollars, which carries 225,000 weekday riders; repairs were combined with hardening against future storms. Format and access: a free article. Licence and cost: free to read. Caveats: a 2016 snapshot from a trade source. Useful for recovery durations and costs in resilience and climate adaptation models of flooded rail tunnels. It relates to the NYC subway coastal storm flood risk case study in the catalogue.
